ai.description: *Rhacophorus subansiriensis* is a 4–5 cm frog with a lime-green dorsum and yellow flanks. It features distinct white spots on the back and translucent, webbing-free fingers. Family: Rhacophoridae.
ai.identificationRemarks: *Rhacophorus subansiriensis* is best distinguished by the distinctive, extensive dark brown reticulated patterns covering its throat and chest, which are absent in similar species.
ai.habitat: The Subansiri Bush Frog inhabits subtropical evergreen forests in Northeast India, typically found at elevations between 300 and 1,500 meters near small, slow-moving streams.
ai.behavior: The Subansiri Bush Frog is primarily nocturnal, remaining camouflaged on vegetation during the day and emerging at night to hunt for small insects.
ai.reproductionNotes: *Rhacophorus subansiriensis* breeds during the monsoon, laying eggs in foam nests attached to vegetation overhanging water. Specific clutch sizes remain undocumented.
ai.distributionRemarks: The Subansiri Bush Frog is endemic to the Lower Subansiri district of Arunachal Pradesh, India, inhabiting tropical evergreen forests at elevations of 300–400 meters.
ai.callDescription: The Subansiri Bush Frog emits a high-pitched, rhythmic "tink-tink" call, typically heard from vegetation near forest streams during the monsoon season.
